\subsection{Smoothing, FPCA, and Classification: Phoneme Data}
\label{subsec:cs1-phoneme}

The phoneme dataset consists of 400 log-periodogram curves recorded across 256
frequency points, representing five phoneme classes (\textit{aa}, \textit{ao},
\textit{dcl}, \textit{iy}, \textit{sh}) with 80 observations each
\citep{ferraty_vieu_2006}.  Each curve is a digitised acoustic spectrum, and
the classification task is to recover the phoneme class from its spectral
shape.  This study demonstrates three core \texttt{fdars} capabilities in
sequence: penalised smoothing, functional principal component analysis (FPCA),
and cross-validated classification.

\paragraph{Smoothing.}
Raw log-periodogram curves carry measurement noise.  We apply GCV-penalised
B-spline smoothing (\texttt{fdars.basis.smooth\_basis\_gcv}) with 15 basis
functions to a representative subset of 20 curves, selecting the penalty
automatically via generalised cross-validation
\citep{craven_wahba_1979,eilers_marx_1996}.
Figure~\ref{fig:cs1-smooth} shows the raw spectra alongside the fitted smooth
curves for each class; the smoothed curves retain the phoneme-specific spectral
peaks while suppressing high-frequency noise.

\paragraph{FPCA.}
FPCA is performed on all 400 curves via \texttt{Fdata.to\_pc(n\_comp=4)}
\citep{ramsay_silverman_2005}.  The first four principal components explain
$[69.3, 23.0, 5.4, 2.3]\%$ of total variance, with the first three components
jointly accounting for 97.7\% of variation.  The scores scatter in
Figure~\ref{fig:cs1-fpca} shows clear class separation in the PC1--PC2 plane,
confirming that the dominant modes of variation align with phoneme identity.

\paragraph{Classification.}
A \texttt{sklearn.\allowbreak pipeline.Pipeline} composed of \texttt{FPCATransformer}
(4 components) and \texttt{FPCLDAClassifier} (linear discriminant analysis on
FPCA scores) is evaluated by 5-fold cross-validation
\citep{preda_saporta_2005}.
The pipeline achieves a mean CV accuracy of 86.3\% on held-out data
(fold scores: $[0.850, 0.850, 0.863, 0.875, 0.875]$), demonstrating that four
functional principal components capture the class-discriminating structure of
the phoneme spectra.
The analysis is reproduced exactly by \texttt{paper/code/casestudy1.py}, which
generates both figures deterministically (re-running the script leaves
\texttt{git diff paper/figures/} empty).

    Light traces: raw curves (3 per class); bold traces: GCV B-spline smoothed
    curves (15 basis functions, penalty selected by GCV\@).  Colours identify
    phoneme classes (\textit{aa}, \textit{ao}, \textit{dcl}, \textit{iy},
    \textit{sh}).}

\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[htbp]

  \caption{FPCA scores scatter for the phoneme data (PC1 vs PC2, colour-coded

  \label{fig:cs1-fpca}
